_meta.title: Companion tool recommendations — third-party AI-productivity tools wired by recommend-tools
_meta.derived_from: ai-kit internal catalog (not vendored from upstream)
_meta.notes: Catalogues the companions branch of /ai:recommend-tools (graphify, caveman, llm-wiki, context7). Each entry documents its tier(s), detection signal, glue file(s), conflict checks, and wiring path. Consumed by `audit-setup-symmetry.sh` so new companions cannot land without a documented wiring path. Companions are orthogonal to MCP/hooks/plugins/subagents — the latter score via `recommend-tools-lib.sh` from stack-signals; companions are surfaced per project judgement and never scored numerically.

recommendations.name: graphify
recommendations.best_for: Brownfield code repos where the agent greps a lot — replaces grep with a scoped subgraph per query
recommendations.value: Knowledge graph at graphify-out/. `graphify query` returns ~60% smaller subgraph than raw grep on multi-file repos.

tiers.name: base
tiers.description: Default tier — query/path/explain over graphify-out/graph.json; no auto-generated wiki. The 'grep → query the graph instead' nudge is NOT a graphify-specific hook: /ai:setup wires bin/hooks/search-delegation-check.sh into every project (Tier A), and that hook emits the graphify message the moment graphify-out/graph.json appears. Nothing to wire here.
tiers.wired_via: workflow/skills/recommend-tools/SKILL.md Phase 3 graphify branch (docs + ignore file); the PreToolUse nudge comes from bin/apply-search-delegation-hook.sh

tiers.name: wiki
tiers.description: Opt-in — `graphify . --wiki` generates graphify-out/wiki/index.md (AST-only, no LLM cost). Useful when the agent does many symbol-lookup grep'ing — wiki is faster than query for navigation.
tiers.post_run_nudge: If graphify-out/ exists without graphify-out/wiki/, recommend re-running with --wiki when the agent's recent transcript shows >3 grep/find calls for symbol locations.

conflicts.warning: graphify-out/wiki/ (AST-derived, opt-in via --wiki) and llm-wiki's wiki/ (curated from raw/ documents) are both called 'wiki'. When both are wired, emit the 'Two wikis present — disambiguation' block in AGENTS.md so the agent never guesses which wiki the user means. See issue #53.

install.notes: Third-party (Graphify-Labs, MIT). The PyPI package is `graphifyy` (double y) while the `graphify` name is being reclaimed upstream; the CLI is still `graphify`. `graphify update .` is AST-only and free; a full `graphify .` calls an LLM extractor and costs real money — never recommend it as the routine refresh.

recommendations.name: caveman
recommendations.best_for: Every project — compressed agent responses (~65% fewer output tokens) plus the cavecrew sub-agents, whose compressed returns keep raw search output out of the main context
recommendations.value: Caveman mode — drops articles/filler/hedging; technical content + code intact. Ships cavecrew-investigator / -builder / -reviewer sub-agents (see subagents.json).
recommendations.risk: Medium — opinionated communication mode, and activation is machine-wide (every project on the machine, not just the target).

tiers.name: base
tiers.description: Universal — auto-prompted by /ai:setup Tier-A Branch 2e. Installs the plugin via the official CLI and writes AGENTS.md glue. Never silently installed: the branch always asks, default yes.
tiers.wired_via: workflow/skills/setup/SKILL.md Branch 2e + bin/apply-caveman.sh + workflow/skills/recommend-tools/SKILL.md Phase 3 caveman branch

tiers.name: activated
tiers.description: Sets caveman's own defaultMode so the mode is explicit and durable rather than resting on caveman's built-in 'full' fallback. Writes {"defaultMode": "full"} into ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/caveman/config.json (merged, never clobbered).

conflicts.warning: caveman's standalone installer copies its hooks into ~/.claude/hooks/ AND writes them into ~/.claude/settings.json, but the plugin manifest already declares the same SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit hooks. A machine that ran both fires every caveman hook twice per event. `bin/apply-caveman.sh` detects this and strips the standalone copies (`--dedupe-only`), leaving the plugin manifest as the single source.

commands: claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman --scope user

recommendations.name: llm-wiki
recommendations.best_for: Projects accumulating non-code documents (PRDs, transcripts, research PDFs, regulation docs) the user re-reads to find things
recommendations.value: Self-maintaining wiki — ingests raw/ documents into interlinked wiki/ pages. The wiki, not raw files, is the artifact that compounds.
recommendations.risk: Low — additive scaffold; agent owns wiki/, never touches raw/.

tiers.name: base
tiers.description: Scaffold wiki/ + raw/ + SCHEMA.md; AGENTS.md pointer.

conflicts.warning: llm-wiki is orthogonal to docs/ — use it for raw-input ingestion (PDFs, transcripts), NOT to migrate existing curated docs. Existing docs/ stays as-is; raw/ is for new untreated source material.
graphify and llm-wiki cover different needs — graphify indexes code, llm-wiki indexes documents. Both can coexist; do not recommend llm-wiki as a code-navigation alternative.

recommendations.name: context7
recommendations.best_for: Any project with third-party library dependencies — code against live docs, not training-data snapshots
recommendations.value: MCP server (project-scope) + optional ~/.claude/rules/context7.md rule. Cuts API hallucinations on third-party libraries.
recommendations.risk: Low — read-only doc lookups, no auto-install of packages.

tiers.name: base
tiers.description: Universal — surfaces for every stack via mcp-servers.json scorer (universal: true). Auto-prompted by /ai:setup Tier-A Branch 2c.
tiers.wired_via: standards/external/mcp-servers.json (scorer-driven) + workflow/skills/recommend-tools/SKILL.md MCP phase + workflow/skills/setup/SKILL.md Branch 2c

detection.any: claude mcp list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi context7 || claude plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi context7
detection.notes: Detection MUST check both — `claude mcp list` only shows user-config MCPs from ~/.claude.json and currently-connected plugin MCPs (so plugin-provided ctx7 is invisible if the plugin isn't enabled in the current project). Adding a user-scope ctx7 when the plugin already provides it triggers Claude Code's 'MCP server skipped — same command/URL' conflict on next /doctor.

conflicts.warning: Plugin already provides context7 MCP. Adding user-scope `claude mcp add context7` causes a 'same command/URL' conflict — Claude Code skips one. Prefer the plugin install (no manual MCP add needed). If user-scope already present and plugin is preferred, remove with `claude mcp remove --scope user context7`.

install.preferred_path: plugin (no manual MCP config needed); user-scope only as fallback when plugin install is unavailable
